subject.title: fix(matrix): tolerate SAS accept events missing method

question: Should OpenClaw accept this private matrix-js-sdk Rust crypto preprocessor wrapper for the SAS missing-method compatibility case, and what proof must be present before merge?
rationale: The code path appears correctly targeted, but the hook is private and sits on Matrix E2EE verification preprocessing, so automation should not decide the boundary acceptance or proof override alone.

options.title: Require Live Matrix Proof First
options.body: Ask for redacted Element/Synapse verification logs, terminal output, linked artifact, or recording from this branch before merging the private preprocessor workaround.

options.title: Accept With Proof Override
options.body: A maintainer can explicitly own the private dependency hook and security-boundary-adjacent risk, then merge with a proof override if live proof is impractical.

options.title: Pause For Upstream Direction
options.body: If the private hook is not acceptable, pause this PR and pursue an upstream matrix-js-sdk or Element compatibility fix instead.

recommendation.title: Require Live Matrix Proof First
recommendation.body: Ask for redacted Element/Synapse verification logs, terminal output, linked artifact, or recording from this branch before merging the private preprocessor workaround.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for Matrix E2EE and verification ownership is in the Matrix SDK and crypto-bootstrap commits connected to this path.
